title: The plating shop returned the job. Why does the production operation still show partial delivery?

visual.title: Four records for 48 valve bodies
rows: 48 arrived, subject to identity and condition checks
PO item linked to the operation
Manually created PO for the same vendor
6 posted at 16 each to a departmental cost centre
96 posted outside the operation’s purchasing reference
Additional 96 relative to the current relevant receipts

refs: SAP ERP · External processing of operations

lead: One production order calls for 48 valve bodies to be machined, plated by an external supplier, and pressure tested back in the plant. All 48 bodies are physically in the plant. The plater has issued a delivery note for 48. The production planner sees the external operation marked as partially delivered. The controller sees only 672 on that operation’s purchasing path at an agreed rate of 16 per body. This is a useful integration failure because three reports can each be internally consistent. To identify the fault, treat the production operation, the purchasing reference and the physical handover as separately identifiable objects, then reconcile them at piece level.
sections:
The plant has retained the bodies through manufacturing. It bought plating work on an identified production operation. The receiving clerk records the supplier’s completed work against the purchase order generated for that operation. This purchasing process differs from a PO to buy 48 finished, independently stocked bodies. SAP’s documented external-processing flow uses an operation control key that allows or prescribes external processing. The routing or order holds the purchasing information. A purchase requisition for the external operation can be converted to a PO item with the operation’s references. Start at the actual production order, even if Engineering can already identify the routing and its expected operation number.

Read the plant, order number, sequence and operation number. Parallel and alternative sequences, rework orders and successive production orders for the same material can make an operation description ambiguous. Find the purchasing reference from the external processing data and follow it to the requisition and the resulting PO item. Record their item numbers. An account assignment containing a valid production order number is useful evidence of the cost destination. By itself it does not establish that the buyer converted the particular requisition generated by the operation. A manually entered order can carry the right supplier, price and description and still follow a different document chain.
Explain what the operation status measures

SAP describes EOPD for an externally processed operation that is partially delivered, and EODL for an external operation that is delivered. These are procurement-related statuses of the operation. A production order may also have operation confirmations, a goods receipt of its final product, inspection results and a technical completion status. Each reports a different part of the business. The planner needs the status on the identified external operation and the history of its purchasing item. A green status at the production order header or a completed vendor delivery note will not by itself explain the receipt quantity associated with the operation.

Under the assumptions here, each accepted piece of external work costs 16 in one currency, the item expects a valuated receipt, and the client has no enhancement that automatically confirms operations on receipt. The standard supplier work receipt charges the production order with actual external processing costs and has a consumption accounting effect. It does not add the corresponding quantity or value to warehouse stock of a finished product. If the plant also manages physical provision of components, follow those separate movements with their own quantities. Counting the same material document once as receipt of plating and once as receipt of finished inventory would create a fictitious output.
Reconstruct the movements that did post

On Monday the supplier brings back 30 bodies. Receiving posts 30 correctly against the PO item that originated with the production operation. On Wednesday the supplier brings the other 18 in two boxes. The clerk posts 12 from the first box against that item and six from the second against a second, manually created PO. This second order, raised during an urgent phone call, carries the same supplier and unit price, but its expense is assigned to a departmental cost centre. It has no purchasing reference to the production operation. There are no reversals, invoices or final-delivery indicators in this example at the point of investigation.

The vendor-facing total is 30 plus 12 plus six, or 48. The relevant operation-facing total is 30 plus 12, or 42. Its corresponding actual charge is 42 times 16, or 672. The departmental receipt accounts for a further six times 16, or 96. Together these reconcile to the commercial expectation of 768 for 48 bodies. These figures support a specific conclusion. Six pieces of actual supplier work were represented by a purchasing event outside the required reference. The physical stockroom count and commercial quantity check both passed because neither required that reference.
Prove that the second receipt belongs to this job

Collect both vendor delivery notes, itemized packing lists and any traveler or serial evidence issued with the bodies. In this example the two boxes on Wednesday are distinguishable by a production traveler and the individual identifiers or lot references recorded at dispatch. Establish that the six bodies match the external operation’s work and agreed rate. The mere existence of another six-piece receipt on the same day is insufficient. A different production order or an approved ad hoc plating order at the same vendor could legitimately have used that amount. If only one vendor note exists for several jobs, ask the shop supervisor to identify the job-level allocation and its checks.

Then read every matching PO history at item level. Display each material document and its signed quantity, value and account assignment. Trace the 96 into the cost centre’s accounting evidence. Search for cancellations or a second receipt on a later date before concluding that the original was still effective at the investigation cutoff. Check whether the vendor has already invoiced either item and whether production has moved the bodies through testing. Those facts affect how teams can correct an erroneous reference without representing another physical delivery or misstating supplier obligations. They also explain why a simple quantity edit is often insufficient.

The first alternative is a unit mismatch. Imagine that the PO is priced per batch of three pieces while Production measures one completed operation per piece. Two batches then represent six pieces, but a report summing raw quantities could show two. Compare the order unit, order price unit, conversion factors and the unit on the material document before matching costs. The incident data uses one piece at 16 throughout, so unit conversion explains none of the variance. Documenting that check is especially useful if the supplier's invoice describes its price per rack or per set while the plant controls individual bodies.

The second alternative is a delivery-completion or tolerance decision. A purchasing item can be considered complete under the business and item settings even though the arithmetic difference from the originally ordered quantity is positive. Equally, a final physical box can be present while the intended item remains outstanding in purchasing history. Review the delivery-completed indicator and the actual final-receipt treatment in the target client. Check the operation status after each relevant action in QA as well as the resulting quantities. A status mismatch with correctly signed receipts on the intended item is a different investigation from six pieces conclusively posted elsewhere.
Select a repair that restores both document chains

A cost reposting of 96 between the cost centre and the production order could change a CO report. It would leave the external operation’s purchasing history at 42, and the unnecessary manual purchasing item would still show its receipt. A manual production confirmation might move an operation status that the scheduler watches while also affecting labor or yield data. Either approach could obscure the evidence of the wrong purchase receipt. The teams should decide whether the incorrect item and receipt can be reversed, which follow-on documents must be dealt with, and which action may correctly record the six completed pieces against the original purchasing reference.

Test the authorized sequence on representative QA documents using the same periods and follow-on state. Quantify the expected end state in advance. In the case with no invoice and no other dependencies, reversing the six-piece erroneous receipt would remove the 96 charge to the cost centre. Recording the verified six against the operation-linked item would take its received quantity to 48 and its external processing cost to 768 at the assumed price. Verify the operation’s delivered status under the client’s final-delivery treatment. Where documents cross a closed accounting period, Finance determines the permissible dates and their consequences. Review the remaining manual PO obligation separately so Purchasing does not leave an unused item available for another receipt.
Design the handover around the operation reference

Put the production order and operation number, linked PO and item, and vendor dispatch identifier on the handover from the shop to Receiving. A printed supplier name and an expected amount alone would have allowed the wrong six-piece posting in this case. If a substitute PO is needed for a legitimate business reason, make Purchasing and Production agree in advance how the operation reference, cost receiver, open quantity and any provisioned components will be handled. A note on the header of a new PO can communicate intent without supplying the operational linkage that the process requires.

A robust regression test posts a partial receipt first and observes both the operation status and the charge. It then processes the balance through the intended reference, verifying the status, receipt quantity and actual costs again. A separate negative test uses an otherwise similar, unrelated item and demonstrates that its receipt has no right to advance the original operation. If a client implements automatic confirmation or a custom interface, record that behavior and retest the distinction there. The defensible support finding identifies the six bodies, their physical receipt, the purchasing item that originally recorded them, and the financial and operational changes that repaired the discrepancy.
